purpose: Identify the holder, waiter and auth-storage phase if the observed 5000 ms startup lock warning repeats in the next disposable native UI run.
scope: Only the existing synthetic native QA build. Production auth source is unchanged.
activationGuards: prepare-native-ui requires CI=true, the QA project URL, QA app environment and exact synthetic transport key; it refuses existing native projects or Metro config.
Native diagnostic factory checks QA environment, expected QA URL, exact synthetic key and identity of the installed synthetic fetch before accessing the filesystem.
Source patch requires exactly one of each of three reviewed anchors and rejects already overlaid source.

fields: active lock operation IDs observed at storage start

semantics: The supplied official processLock remains the underlying lock implementation with its original name and timeout arguments.
Original receiver and callback arguments are forwarded; resolved value references and rejection error objects are preserved.
Promise settlement observers return their rejection chain so ignored rejected operations are not converted into successful results.
No auth callback, timeout, refresh policy, network route or provider credential is substituted by the diagnostic.

bounds.retention: First 512 startup events plus most recent 512 events, with dropped-event count.
bounds.pendingPolicy: Replace with latest snapshot while one serialized write is pending. A failed write does not block the latest snapshot.

evidenceIntegration.overlayManifest: native-ui-logs/source.json includes original/after hashes and retained exact overlay content.
evidenceIntegration.workflowTrigger: New helper native-ui-auth-overlay.cjs matches existing scripts/quality/*native-ui* path filter; workflow itself unchanged.
evidenceIntegration.collection: Both iOS and Android collect trace on successful completion and in cleanup after failures.
evidenceIntegration.filesystem: Native expo-file-system/legacy writes, separate from observed AsyncStorage.

covered: Actual pinned processLock preserves exclusion and correlates active holder, queued operation and pending storage.
Original arguments, receivers, resolved references and rejection objects are retained.
Timeout/error paths do not run unauthorized work or serialize private error data.
Snapshot privacy is tested with sentinel lock names, storage keys, session values and errors.
Bounded startup/latest retention and ID limits.
Clock or sink failure does not change auth result.
Production/real-provider/wrong-transport configurations fail closed before filesystem access.
Stalled and failed disk writes coalesce to one latest snapshot and cannot overwrite out of order.
Actual disposable preparation verifies source before/after/retained hashes and leaves production file unchanged.
verification.shellSyntax: bash -n passes for both native UI shell scripts

reviews.nativeAcceptanceAgent: Final integration review acknowledged no blocker: import order, filesystem paths, success/cleanup extraction, source hashes and workflow trigger.
reviews.root: Accepted recorder and bounded writer; timings are explicitly diagnostic, not uninstrumented production performance.

limitations: Next Android/iOS emulator execution has not yet produced this trace. These local harness results do not resolve the earlier warning.
Observer microtasks and native filesystem writes add overhead; trace durations diagnose lock/storage phases and must not be advertised as uninstrumented production performance.
Numeric IDs correlate SDK lock activity with active auth-storage operations; they do not expose or infer private storage contents or a named high-level auth command.
Only the auth client storage adapter is observed; unrelated application AsyncStorage use is not globally instrumented.
A missing or interrupted trace remains missing evidence, not a passing lock diagnosis.
